evidence: At 0x40118a buffer is 32 bytes at rbp-0x20
At 0x40118e rsi is set to argv[1]
PoC input of 64 A's causes SIGSEGV

plan.root_cause: handle copies argv[1] into a 32-byte stack buffer with unbounded strcpy; inputs of 32 bytes or more overwrite the saved frame.

edits.reason: Redirect the original strcpy call to the guard stub at 0x401211.
Guard loop validates printable ASCII length 0..31; valid path calls original strcpy and returns; invalid path writes invalid_stderr and exits 1.
Exact invalid_stderr bytes used by the invalid path.

stub.source:
push rdi
mov rdi, rsi
xor ecx, ecx
.loop:
  cmp ecx, 32
  je invalid
  mov al, [rdi]
  test al, al
  je valid
  cmp al, 0x20
  jb invalid
  cmp al, 0x7e
  ja invalid
  inc rdi
  inc ecx
  jmp .loop
.valid:
  pop rdi
  call strcpy@plt
  ret
.invalid:
  pop rdi
  mov edi, 2
  lea rsi, [rip + invalid_stderr]
  mov edx, 42
  mov eax, 1
  syscall
  mov eax, 60
  mov edi, 1
  syscall

plan.valid_path: The guard scans the input byte-by-byte until NUL. If all bytes before NUL are printable ASCII and the length is 0..31, it pops the saved buffer pointer, calls the original strcpy@plt, and returns to the original puts sequence in handle.
plan.invalid_path: If length reaches 32 before NUL, or any byte is non-printable, the guard pops the saved buffer pointer, writes the exact 42-byte invalid_stderr string to fd 2 with syscall write, then exits with status 1 via syscall exit. It does not touch stdout.

stated_criteria_coverage.how: The loop allows strcpy only when the length is <=31; strcpy writes at most 32 bytes including the terminating NUL into the 32-byte buffer at rbp-0x20.
The guard rejects length 32 before the NUL at index 32 can be written, so the terminating NUL is never written past buf[31].
The loop compares the length counter to 32 before reading each byte; length 31 is accepted and length 32 is rejected.

stated_criteria_coverage.criterion: valid_domain: printable ASCII, length 0..31, no NUL
stated_criteria_coverage.how: Each byte before NUL is checked against 0x20..0x7e; the loop stops at NUL so the string length is the number of printable bytes before NUL and is bounded by 31.

stated_criteria_coverage.criterion: valid_behavior: write the input followed by a single LF to stdout; exit 0
stated_criteria_coverage.how: On valid input the guard calls the original strcpy and returns to 0x401199; the original puts call writes the input plus LF, and main still returns 0.

stated_criteria_coverage.criterion: forbidden_behavior: any write past buf[31], including the terminating NUL
stated_criteria_coverage.how: The guard prevents strcpy execution for length >=32, so no copy occurs beyond the buffer; valid strcpy writes at most up to buf[31].

stated_criteria_coverage.criterion: invalid_response: write exactly the bytes of invalid_stderr to fd 2; exit 1; write nothing to stdout; do not crash
stated_criteria_coverage.how: The invalid path uses syscall write with fd=2, rsi pointing to the exact invalid_stderr data, rdx=42, then syscall exit with status 1. It never calls puts or strcpy on invalid input.
The data at 0x401300 contains exactly those 42 ASCII bytes; the invalid path references it with RIP-relative lea.

assumptions: Bytes from 0x401211 through 0x4012ff in the R-X segment are unused padding and can be used for added code and data.
The binary runs in a Linux x86-64 environment where syscall uses the standard ABI.
The existing strcpy@plt and puts@plt behave according to standard C semantics.
argv[1] is a normal C string with no embedded NUL bytes.
The invalid_stderr string length is exactly 42 bytes.
uncertainties: The exact original bytes in the unused R-X tail are not shown in the disassembly; the plan assumes they are zeros or can be overwritten.
The contract SHA-256 and prompt SHA-256 were not provided in the prompt; zero placeholders are used.
The plan has not been executed or tested; acceptance depends on a deterministic verifier checking the listed edits against the actual binary.
